mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.7% triggers a loss of investor confidence in labor market stability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in triggered instances are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or UNRATE does not cross the threshold within the specified period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in the federal funds rate and growth in economic demand (GDPC1) signal accommodative monetary policy, amplifying equity valuation growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 does not correlate with positive 60-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over 5-year window).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion phase, a decline in the federal funds rate is expected to have a stronger positive impact on S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced policy tightness.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained inflationary pressure indicated by CPIAUCSL exceeding 200.0 triggers investor concerns about future rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in inflationary periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or CPIAUCSL does not cross the threshold within the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) and housing demand (HOUST) both increasing signal robust economic growth, which expands corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of INDPRO and HOUST does not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trajectory in the unemployment rate beyond 4.7% indicates weakening labor market conditions, reducing growth expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rising unemployment periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or UNRATE does not rise steadily over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in demand-side economic activity measured by RSAFS exceeding 400,000 units triggers increased corporate investment and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in triggered instances are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or RSAFS does not cross the threshold within the 5-day window.
